title: Evaluation of machine learning-based prediction of pregnancy complications and adverse birth outcomes using routine data.
summary: Using 442,760 Kaiser Permanente Northern California pregnancies, separate XGBoost models predicted gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes and pre-eclampsia at 12 weeks; prediction of four adverse birth outcomes was weaker. Transfer to a 6,105-pregnancy cohort required local tuning, and cost-effectiveness was modeled rather than an intervention trial.
ai_technology: XGBoost models trained on longitudinal electronic health records
